title: Jailed in Memphis over the Drifters booking
summary: He was jailed in Memphis after booking the wrong Drifters group, then won a settlement.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and the Prohibition-era clubs

blocks.x: Okay, well I can see that, but I'm just stuck in saying in general, when you knew that you were going out, sending a band out on the road, that you could get a phone call. Did you ever get any phone calls, hey I'm in jail. No, no, no. Who's going to arrest you? I got put in jail once though.

Oh, yeah. In Tennessee. Yeah, I got put in jail once. But it was, they had two set of drifters. They had the old region, which is, this is the old region up here. Yeah. That's them right there. That's them right there. And then the new one came out. So we had played the new one when they first came out. So when the new one came out, Shaw booked them. Shaw booked. And we were still booking these here. The only mistake we made in putting in the contract, we should have put the old drifters in the contract. So a fraternity is, sorority, which is the women's? Is it sorority or sorority?

Well, the male, the male booked us in Memphis, Tennessee. So when we got there, we was in the restaurant and the police came in and they wanted to see the band leader. So I was with them. So when he went outside, I went outside with him, because he was a young boy too, you know. If anything's going wrong, I'm going to take care of it, you know. So then they told him what happened. So I said, well no, you don't take him. I said, let him go. I'll go, I'll go, I'll go, take him. So I went inside and told the band leader that I was going to see. I told him to set up with him, so I went on with him. So we went to court, that was on a Saturday. So they canceled the gig, got hit, and the head was canceled. So I said, the band came back to New Orleans. And Sunday, I stayed in jail Saturday night, and Sunday went to court Monday. So they came back in and got me some pictures of the new drifters and the old drifters. They sent them to me, especially over to the jail. They said, I got there, and they said, the band did that. When I went to court, I showed the jury what the set up was. I said, I had his two pictures, and both pictures have drifters on it. I said, this is a set of drifters that these boys bought. And I said, this is a set they didn't buy. This is a set who got the suit against them. So the judge, he sat there and looked at the pictures. He told them, he said, you don't have a case. He said, the name booked you some drifters all right. He didn't book you no phone. He booked you drifters on it. It's called these two pictures I got in. They both got drifters on it. I said, you just got another set.

So then my lawyer told me he wanted to get a suit against them. And so then I cried and I said, I guess it makes sense. So they got together, and I got $250 to give me a train ticket to the New Orleans. So a hundred and quarter night in jail wasn't too bad. It wasn't too bad. But he wanted to go through. I said, no, just take the two fifths and forget it. You take a hundred dollars and give me a hundred and fifty dollars and you get out of there and go on. He wanted to go on the court and whatever. So we really had him over the bow. What they should have did, they should have quescent me before arresting me. Of course they wouldn't arrest me to arrest the band leader. But he was too young and I took the fifths. But that's the only case we ever had with jail business.
Everybody's got that story about jail on the road.

Well, I don't dispute that. I think there's a lot of musicians who go to jail on the road. I think this happens. Yeah. But in my deal I never had to travel with them. A lot of time I'd travel with them, you see, and I kept them straight.
